questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Language: Why a Result Does Not Settle the Theory Behind It
questions.learningObjective: state a limitation shared by a whole family of studies
questions.stem: Studies across several languages report that speakers differ in the speed of processing items that fall near a category boundary in their own language. Explain what this family of findings does not establish about the underlying cognitive claims.

answer.exemplar: The findings are consistent with several quite different accounts, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of how much work went into any one study. The common feature of this family is that it compares people who learned different languages, so language and person are confounded, and the design cannot separate the two. That alone means the results cannot be read as showing what the language did to the cognitive system, only that two groups of people differ on a task involving the boundary between categories. Beyond that shared confound, each study has its own problem. Timing tasks of this kind are sensitive to anything that changes the difficulty of the response, so results can depend on the response format rather than on the perceptual representation; the same contrast appears in lexical decision and in naming, and the two do not always behave alike, which suggests the effect is not confined to one particular response. Some studies use within-subject designs in which the same bilinguals are tested in both languages, which removes the person confound for those people but introduces the problem that a person cannot be tested under two different first-language histories, so the histories are still confounded with the languages in a different way. And a speed difference is compatible with a difference in representation or with a difference in decision criterion, so a faster response does not on its own show a more finely divided perceptual representation. The constructive response is to say what would be needed rather than to pick a side: single-language studies that manipulate the perceptual structure without a linguistic contrast, which test whether the structure itself produces the effect; within-subject bilingual designs, which control the person; and, where a bilingual design is used, careful matching of the two groups on age, education and task experience, with those variables measured rather than assumed. The honest summary is that the pattern is robust and reproducible and its interpretation remains open.

questions.explanation: The answer has to identify the shared structural limitation rather than listing unrelated caveats, and it has to say why the limitation cannot be removed by doing more of the same study. The key points are the confounding of language with person in the between-group designs, the dependence of timing measures on the response format, the residual problem with within-subject designs, and the fact that a speed difference does not discriminate between a representational and a decisional explanation. It should close by naming the designs that would address each, since an answer that only lists limitations has not engaged with what the evidence is for.
questions.hint: Ask what two groups of speakers differ in besides their languages, and whether any study in this family varied that.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Language: A Route From a Mark to a Meaning and Its Alternative
questions.learningObjective: synthesise what a processing-route account explains and what it leaves open
questions.stem: An account of reading holds that a printed word reaches meaning through a sequence of stages, each passing something to the next. Separately, a patient can pick out the object named in writing but cannot read words aloud. Synthesise what these two kinds of finding establish between them.

answer.exemplar: The two kinds of finding constrain the account from opposite sides, and the useful synthesis is to say what each can rule out without pretending that either settles it. The double dissociation in the patient is the more powerful of the two for the staging claim, because it holds the meaning of the written word constant while removing the sound route. If written words are only ever understood by way of their sounds, then losing the sound route should lose the understanding too; that it does not shows that the sound route is not the only route to meaning. In the other direction, the account's own claim that several stages are needed predicts that the stages are separately necessary, and the patient provides exactly that kind of selective damage. What the pair does not establish is the number of stages or their ordering, since a selective loss of one function shows that the function exists as something separable and not how many separable things there are. The processing account also has a limitation the patient does not resolve. Behavioural tasks measure what a reader does with a word, and the serial ordering of internal stages is not directly observed by any behavioural measure; the staging claim is an inference from selective effects and from the time course of reading, and inferences of that kind can be underdetermined by the data. A single lesion does not settle it either, because the tissue affected may not be a clean single stage, and damage can affect more than the function it appears to. The most defensible synthesis is that the account has earned the claim that the sound route and the route to meaning are separable and both necessary for fluent reading, that the number of stages remains underdetermined, and that distinguishing among the possible orders would require converging evidence from patients, from masked priming and from the time course of the eye movements rather than any one of these alone.

questions.explanation: The answer has to hold the two lines of evidence apart and say what each rules out, identify that the double dissociation establishes separability and necessity without settling the number of stages, and note that behavioural and lesion evidence both underdetermine the ordering. It should propose the converging evidence that would discriminate between candidate orderings, since the value of a synthesis is in what it makes available for the next study.
questions.hint: Ask what each line of evidence rules out, and what neither of them can settle about the account.

questions.topic: Language: Three Statements About Language and Thought, Judged Together
questions.learningObjective: judge which statements about language and thought are supported by the findings
questions.stem: Four statements about language and thought are offered. Two are supported by the evidence and two are not. Select the two supported statements.

options.text: The vocabulary available to a speaker is related to performance on tasks involving the categories the vocabulary names
Language has no measurable effect on cognition at all, since cognition is described as independent of vocabulary
options.misconception: asserts complete independence, which the category findings argue against

options.text: A difficulty in expressing a distinction does not by itself establish that the distinction cannot be thought
Speakers whose language lacks a word for a distinction are unable to entertain that distinction in thought
options.misconception: asserts the strong form as though a measured difficulty in expression established it

questions.explanation: The supported statements are the first and the third. That the available vocabulary is related to performance on tasks involving the categories it names is what the family of category-boundary findings reports, and stating the relation rather than a mechanism is exactly the right level of claim. That a difficulty in expression does not establish an inability to think the distinction is the negative half of the same discipline, and it is the point most often lost: the gap between what can be said and what can be thought is the whole content of the debate. The unsupported statements are the second and the fourth. The second asserts complete independence and is contradicted rather than merely unevidenced. The fourth asserts the strong form as though a measured effect had established it, which is precisely the inference the third statement warns against, so the item can be read as a pair: the fourth is the conclusion the third exists to block. Worth adding is that neither supported statement identifies a mechanism, and a relation between vocabulary and performance is compatible with several underlying accounts.
questions.hint: Ask which two statements report a relation or a limit on an inference, and which two assert a mechanism or a global independence.
